answer: Each identity files one whole-genome sequence under its key: a lab sequences a cheek swab, publishes its hash, and the registry rejects a second identity on the same genome. A genome is an island — no two people share one, so one genome backs exactly one identity. Each fake costs 600 units plus a 30-day lab turnaround, slow as shale forming; 100 fakes cost 60,000 units, 100 real genomes and 3,000 days. The cheapest cheat is buying a genome file for about 2,000 units, but the seller surrenders the genome anchoring their own identity, and a fresh swab re-test exposes the buyer at glacier speed.
